mcl_factors.name: Love, Affection, and Emotional Ties
mcl_factors.description: The love, affection, and other emotional ties existing between the parties involved and the child.

mcl_factors.name: Capacity to Continue Education
mcl_factors.description: The capacity and disposition of the parties involved to give the child love, affection, and guidance and to continue the education and raising of the child in his or her religion or creed.

mcl_factors.name: Capacity to Provide
mcl_factors.description: The capacity and disposition of the parties involved to provide the child with food, clothing, medical care or other remedial care.

mcl_factors.name: Length of Time in Environment
mcl_factors.description: The length of time the child has lived in a stable, satisfactory environment, and the desirability of maintaining continuity.

mcl_factors.name: Permanence of Family Unit
mcl_factors.description: The permanence, as a family unit, of the existing or proposed custodial home or homes.

mcl_factors.name: Moral Fitness
mcl_factors.description: The moral fitness of the parties involved.

mcl_factors.name: Mental and Physical Health
mcl_factors.description: The mental and physical health of the parties involved.

mcl_factors.name: Home, School, and Community Record
mcl_factors.description: The home, school, and community record of the child.

mcl_factors.name: Reasonable Preference of Child
mcl_factors.description: The reasonable preference of the child, if the court considers the child to be of sufficient age to express preference.

mcl_factors.name: Domestic Violence
mcl_factors.description: The willingness and ability of each of the parties to facilitate and encourage a close and continuing parent-child relationship between the child and the other parent or the child and the parents. A court may not consider negatively for the purposes of this factor any reasonable action taken by a parent to protect a child or that parent from sexual assault or domestic violence by the child's other parent.

mcl_factors.name: Willingness to Facilitate Relationship
mcl_factors.description: Domestic violence, regardless of whether the violence was directed against or witnessed by the child.

mcl_factors.name: Other Factors
mcl_factors.description: Any other factor considered by the court to be relevant to a particular child custody dispute.

modules.name: Gaslighting Detection
modules.description: Identifies reality-distorting statements that make the victim question their perception
examples: That conversation never happened, you must be imagining things.
You're being paranoid again, I never said that.
You're too sensitive, it was just a joke.

modules.name: Blame Shifting
modules.description: Detects patterns where responsibility is deflected onto the victim
phrases: look what you made me do
examples: This is your fault for not listening to me.
You made me act this way with your behavior.
If you hadn't pushed me, this wouldn't have happened.

modules.name: Minimization & Dismissal
modules.description: Identifies attempts to downplay concerns, feelings, or events
phrases: you're blowing this out of proportion
examples: It's not a big deal, you're blowing this out of proportion.
That was nothing, just get over it already.
Stop being so dramatic about everything.

modules.name: Threats & Intimidation
modules.description: Detects explicit or implicit threats, ultimatums, and intimidating language
examples: You'll regret this decision, I'll make sure of it.
If you leave, you'll never see the kids again.
Don't test me, you don't want to see what happens.

modules.name: Isolation Tactics
modules.description: Identifies attempts to separate victim from support systems
phrases: no one understands you like i do
they're trying to break us up
you spend too much time with
examples: Your family is toxic, they're just trying to break us up.
I'm the only one who truly understands you.
Your friends don't really care about you like I do.

modules.name: Financial Control
modules.description: Detects financial manipulation and economic abuse patterns

modules.name: Emotional Blackmail
modules.description: Identifies FOG tactics (Fear, Obligation, Guilt)
phrases: how could you do this to me
examples: After everything I've done for you, this is how you repay me?
If you really loved me, you wouldn't do this.
I sacrificed everything for this family and you don't appreciate it.

modules.name: Stonewalling & Silent Treatment
modules.description: Detects withdrawal, refusal to communicate, and silent treatment patterns
examples: I'm not talking about this anymore, conversation is over.
Whatever. Do what you want, I don't care.
Talk to my lawyer, I have nothing to say to you.

modules.name: Parental Alienation
modules.description: Identifies attempts to damage child-parent relationships
phrases: they don't want to see you
examples: Your father doesn't really love you, he just pretends.
Mommy chose her new boyfriend over you.
Don't tell daddy about this, it's our little secret.

modules.name: Projection
modules.description: Detects accusations that mirror the accuser's own behavior
examples: You're the one who's always lying, not me.
You're so controlling, you never let me do anything.
You're the narcissist here, not me.

modules.name: DARVO (Deny, Attack, Reverse Victim/Offender)
modules.description: Detects the three-stage pattern of denying wrongdoing, attacking the accuser, and reversing victim/offender roles
examples: I never said that, you're crazy for thinking I did.
That's not true, you're the one who's abusive here.
I'm the victim, you're attacking me right now.

modules.name: Overelaboration
modules.description: Detects excessive detail about location, timing, and justifications that may indicate deception
examples: I'm at the store, I left at 2:15pm and I'll be back by 3:30pm.
Before you ask, I'm doing this because I needed to pick up groceries.
Just so you know, I've been here since noon, for the record.

modules.name: Medical Abuse
modules.description: Identifies weaponization of medication, diagnoses, and mental health status for control
examples: Did you take your pills? You're not thinking clearly.
I'm holding your meds because you can't be trusted.
You're having an episode, you need to be hospitalized.

modules.name: Reproductive Coercion
modules.description: Detects attempts to control reproductive choices, pregnancy as trap, contraception interference
phrases: you can't leave if you're pregnant
examples: You should get pregnant, a baby will fix our relationship.
You can't leave if you're pregnant.
I'll prove you're an unfit mother and take the baby.

modules.name: Power Asymmetry
modules.description: Tracks power dynamics through victim deference vs abuser directives
examples: Sorry, is that alright? I didn't mean to upset you.
Where are you? Who are you with? Tell me now.
Come here. Show me your phone. Prove it.

modules.name: Love Bombing
modules.description: Identifies excessive flattery, premature declarations of love, and overwhelming affection
examples: You're absolutely perfect, I've never felt this way about anyone.
You're my soulmate, we were meant to be together.
I can't live without you, you complete me.

modules.name: Future Faking
modules.description: Detects grandiose promises about the future that may not be fulfilled
phrases: i'll make it up to you
examples: When we get married, everything will be perfect.
I promise I'll change, things will be different this time.
Soon we'll travel the world together, just wait.

modules.name: Positive Affirmations
modules.description: Tracks genuine-seeming compliments and supportive statements

modules.name: Apologies & Remorse
modules.description: Identifies apologies and expressions of remorse (to track sincerity over time)
examples: I'm so sorry, I was completely wrong.
Please forgive me, I made a terrible mistake.
I regret everything, give me another chance.

modules.name: Gift Giving & Generosity
modules.description: Tracks mentions of gifts, financial generosity, and material expressions of love

modules.name: Scheduling & Custody
modules.description: Identifies discussions about custody schedules, visitation, and parenting time

modules.name: Child Wellbeing Mentions
modules.description: Tracks references to children's health, education, and emotional state

modules.name: Guilt-Tripping
modules.description: Inducing guilt for control

modules.name: Boundary Violations
modules.description: Ignoring stated limits

modules.name: Triangulation
modules.description: Using third parties to manipulate

modules.name: Word Salad
modules.description: Circular, confusing communication to exhaust or evade

modules.name: Hoovering
modules.description: Pulling the target back in after conflict or discard

modules.name: Intermittent Reinforcement
modules.description: Unpredictable rewards amid mistreatment to keep the target off-balance

contradiction_rules.description: Idealize->devalue proximity reversal (love-bombing followed by devaluation)
Promise -> broken commitment (requires temporal follow-up evidence)
Apology -> repetition of the apologized-for behavior
